name: Katherine M. Clark

data_centers.summary: No public statements on data centers found as of Sept 2026. She voted against the Republican SPEED Act permitting bill in December 2025, but that was a party-line vote on a broad permitting bill, not a stated position on data centers.

evidence.title: House roll call 356 (Dec 18 2025): H.R.4776 SPEED Act permitting reform, Clark voted Nay
evidence.what_it_shows: A Nay on a Republican permitting bill that Democrats broadly opposed; it is not a stated position on data centers.

ai_risk.summary: Searched her official site, whip statements, interviews, letters and campaign coverage and found no public position on AI safety or AI regulation as of Sept 2026. Leads tying her to an xAI Grok investigation, an AI super PAC endorsement and the House AI Task Force all turned out to be about Rep. Yvette Clarke of New York.

tech_regulation.summary: Her tech record is old and narrow. As a rank-and-file member she wrote bills against online harassment, swatting and sextortion, and in 2024 she voted against the TikTok divestiture bill without a public explanation. No recent Big Tech, privacy or kids online safety statements were found.

evidence.title: Press release: Clark, Brooks, Meehan introduce the bipartisan Online Safety Modernization Act
evidence.quote: We need to make sure that our policies keep up with the realities of our connected world.
evidence.what_it_shows: She has a history of writing targeted federal rules against online crimes like sextortion, doxxing and swatting.

evidence.title: Official page: Clark proposals to combat online abuse (Prioritizing Online Threats Enforcement Act, Interstate Swatting Hoax Act)
evidence.quote: Congresswoman Katherine Clark has championed combatting severe online threats and abuse.
evidence.what_it_shows: Her office lists a set of bills aimed at online threats against women, a targeted approach rather than broad platform regulation.

evidence.title: House roll call 86 (Mar 13 2024): H.R.7521 Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act (TikTok divestiture), Clark voted Nay
evidence.what_it_shows: She opposed the bill forcing TikTok's sale or ban; no statement explaining the vote was found, so her reasoning is unclear.

evidence.title: Press release: Whip Clark, House Democrats introduce the Taxpayer Data Protection Act
evidence.quote: a bill to prevent unlawful access to Americans’ most sensitive personal information
evidence.what_it_shows: Aimed at Elon Musk's DOGE team accessing Treasury data; it concerns government data privacy rather than regulating tech companies.

preemption.summary: No statement found on federal preemption or a moratorium on state AI laws. She did not sign the Nov 26 2025 Matsui letter or the Dec 3 2025 Clarke letter against a state AI law moratorium; both signer lists were checked directly.

china_chips.summary: No statements or bills found on AI chip export controls, Nvidia sales to China or DeepSeek as of Sept 2026.

signature: No notable public AI activity found; the House Democratic Whip's tech record is limited to decade-old online harassment bills and a 2024 vote against the TikTok divestiture bill.
search_notes: Ran about 14 Google News queries (AI, data centers, chatbot/deepfake, Big Tech/Section 230, Nvidia/export controls, preemption, KOSA, TikTok, Musk/Grok, jobs, interviews) plus a full archived listing of katherineclark.house.gov and democraticwhip.gov; nothing AI-specific surfaced. Opened the E&C Grok investigation release, the Sludge super PAC article and the AI Civil Rights Act materials: all refer to Rep. Yvette D. Clarke (NY-9), not Katherine Clark, so those three landscape leads were discarded. Extracted the Matsui letter PDF text and the Clarke NDAA letter and the Casar AI CEO letter: Clark is not a signer of any. Verified TikTok and SPEED Act votes on govtrack. Google News URL decoding was rate limited (429) for most of the session, so several headlines (CBS Boston TikTok delegation story) could not be opened.

name: Seth Moulton

data_centers.summary: Mixed by design. Moulton rejects a data center moratorium and says blocking data centers would cede AI leadership to China, but he also wants 'tight restrictions' so data centers do not raise electricity bills or drain water, and he signed two House Democratic letters pressing regulators and industry on ratepayer costs.

evidence.title: Tufts Daily interview: Moulton asked whether Congress should pause data center construction
evidence.quote: we can’t have data centers coming in and just raising everybody’s electricity bills and taking everybody’s water and everything else. But to basically cede leadership on AI to China would be incredibly dangerous
evidence.what_it_shows: Asked about a Sanders-style moratorium, he refused to pause construction but said data centers must not push costs onto households.

evidence.title: Tufts Daily interview: Moulton on AI companies and communities
evidence.quote: That doesn’t mean that we should give free reign to the AI companies. I think there should be tight restrictions on what they’re able to do in our communities.
evidence.what_it_shows: He pairs support for AI growth with a call for tight local restrictions on AI companies.

evidence.title: Letter from 20 House Democrats led by Rep. Kevin Mullin to FERC, Edison Electric Institute and the Data Center Coalition on data center energy costs (Moulton co-signed)
evidence.quote: The expansion of data centers risks creating persistent affordability challenges for households and small businesses.
evidence.what_it_shows: He joined colleagues asking regulators, utilities and the industry how grid upgrade costs will be kept off household bills.

evidence.title: New Democrat Coalition letter to House appropriators requesting a DOE National Strategic Data Center Plan (Moulton signed)
evidence.quote: Rapidly increasing demand for data centers, driven by cloud computing and AI, is vital for America's economy and competitiveness. However, this expansion strains electricity grids, land, water, and community infrastructure
evidence.what_it_shows: Frames data centers as vital but calls for managed growth and a national plan covering grid, water and consumer cost impacts.

evidence.title: House roll call 356 (Dec 18 2025): H.R.4776 SPEED Act permitting reform, Moulton voted Nay
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted against the Republican permitting bill that supporters said would speed energy and data center projects.

ai_risk.summary: Moulton says AI is here to stay and America should lead it, but he wants protections around AI tools, has backed targeted rules (no AI control of nuclear launches, bans on AI election lies) and says government must be ready to help workers displaced by AI. He does not talk about AI as an existential danger.

evidence.title: WCVB debate coverage: Moulton attacks Markey's AI answer in the final Senate primary debate
evidence.quote: if you don't even know what you're using on your phone or your iPad, like this is why we need a new generation of leaders to regulate these technologies
evidence.what_it_shows: He framed regulating AI as necessary and cast himself as the generation that should write the rules.

evidence.title: New Bedford Light debate coverage: Moulton on using AI tools
evidence.quote: These are tools that can help, but they’re also tools that need protections
evidence.what_it_shows: He says he uses AI himself and supports protections around it.

evidence.title: Tufts Daily interview: Moulton on AI job displacement
evidence.quote: we need to be prepared for massive disruptions in our economy.
evidence.what_it_shows: He agrees with Rep. Ro Khanna that government should be ready to help workers, such as paralegals, who lose jobs to AI.

evidence.title: 118th H.R.2894 Block Nuclear Launch by Autonomous Artificial Intelligence Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed a rule that a human, not an AI, must make any nuclear launch decision.

evidence.title: 119th H.R.4894 Deceptive Practices and Voter Intimidation Prevention Act of 2025 (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports banning AI-made lies about voting in the two months before a federal election.

evidence.title: 119th H.R.2385 CREATE AI Act of 2025 (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a public computing resource so researchers can build AI, a pro-innovation measure.

evidence.title: Press release: Moulton joins Hurd, Kelly resolution to create a national AI strategy
evidence.quote: I'd rather the future be defined by our values, not theirs.
evidence.what_it_shows: Early framing of AI as a race with China and Russia that America must lead.

tech_regulation.summary: Moulton wants more accountability for big tech companies and has cosponsored a long list of targeted bills: the Kids Online Safety Act, kids privacy updates, Sammy's Law, hidden-camera disclosure for smart devices, reproductive data privacy and the TikTok divestiture. He is a founding member of the Congressional Antitrust Caucus but has not called for break-ups or repealing Section 230.

evidence.title: Brookline.News joint interview: Moulton on surveillance technology and regulating AI
evidence.quote: It just went too far in saying, ‘Hey, this is just a laissez-faire world where there’s no accountability.’
evidence.what_it_shows: He criticized the hands-off 1996 Telecommunications Act and said Congress left too little accountability for major technology companies.

evidence.title: 118th H.R.7891 Kids Online Safety Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed the House version of KOSA requiring apps to protect kids from harmful content and addictive design.

evidence.title: 119th H.R.2657 Sammy's Law (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would make big social media sites let parents use safety apps to monitor kids' accounts.

evidence.title: 119th H.R.859 Informing Consumers about Smart Devices Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would require disclosure when a smart device contains a hidden camera or microphone.

evidence.title: House roll call 86 (Mar 13 2024): H.R.7521 TikTok divestiture bill, Moulton voted Yea (he was also a cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: He voted to force TikTok's Chinese owner to sell or face a ban.

evidence.title: Press release: Moulton, Congressional Antitrust Caucus lead letter to FTC on corporate consolidation
evidence.what_it_shows: As a founding member of the Congressional Antitrust Caucus he asked the FTC to review how consolidation hurts workers, consumers and small businesses.

preemption.summary: In a July 2026 interview Moulton said states should be allowed to adopt their own AI rules while Congress writes broader federal standards. He did not sign the two Nov and Dec 2025 House Democratic letters opposing a state AI law moratorium, and no direct quote on preemption was found.

evidence.title: Brookline.News joint interview: Moulton on state versus federal AI regulation (reporter's summary)
evidence.quote: Moulton said he supports allowing states to adopt their own AI regulations while Congress develops broader federal standards.
evidence.what_it_shows: A reporter's paraphrase, not his own words, but it places him against blocking state AI laws before federal rules exist.

china_chips.summary: Moulton sits on the House China Select Committee and has cosponsored bills to block the most powerful chips from going to China and to remove DeepSeek from government devices, and he says ceding AI leadership to China would be dangerous. No statement on the Nvidia H20 or H200 sales was found.

evidence.title: 119th H.R.5022 No Advanced Chips for the CCP Act of 2025 (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would block the most powerful AI chips from being sold to China.

evidence.title: 119th H.R.1121 No DeepSeek on Government Devices Act (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would remove the Chinese AI app DeepSeek from federal devices.

evidence.title: Tufts Daily interview: Moulton on AI competition with China
evidence.quote: to basically cede leadership on AI to China would be incredibly dangerous to the United States of America
evidence.what_it_shows: He treats the AI race with China as a national security matter.

signature: Lost the Sept 1 2026 Senate primary to Markey after making generational leadership on AI regulation a campaign theme; a New Democrat who says America must lead on AI but wants tight restrictions on data centers and AI companies.

notable_quote.text: With all due respect, Senator, if you don't even know what you're using on your phone or your iPad, like this is why we need a new generation of leaders to regulate these technologies

groups: New Democrat Coalition (member; signed its March 2026 data center letter)
Congressional Artificial Intelligence Caucus (member per first-pass landscape research; membership page could not be reached to verify)
search_notes: Ran about 16 Google News queries (AI, data centers, chatbot/deepfake/Big Tech, Nvidia/chips/DeepSeek, preemption/moratorium, campaign AI plan, defense AI donors, debates) and archived listings of moulton.house.gov and sethmoulton.com. Opened and quoted the Tufts Daily (Mar 6 2026), Brookline.News (Jul 14 2026), WCVB (Aug 20 2026) and New Bedford Light (Aug 21 2026) pieces. Confirmed his signature on the Mullin FERC letter (Beyer release) and, by extracting the PDF text, on the New Dem data center letter; confirmed he is NOT on the Matsui, Clarke or Casar letters. Verified TikTok (Yea) and SPEED Act (Nay) votes on govtrack; verified he is an original cosponsor of the Energy Bills Relief Act (H.R.7977) but could not confirm that bill addresses data centers, so it is not used. Could not open his campaign AI policy page (sethmoulton.com/issue/ai-policy, Cloudflare block; Wayback unreachable), the CNBC Aug 27 2026 story 'AI bursts to the front of Massachusetts Democratic Senate primary', or the Sept 1 2026 techtimes piece on defense AI donations versus Anthropic money, because Google News URL decoding was rate limited; no AI super PAC evidence was therefore recorded.

name: Ayanna Pressley

data_centers.summary: In July 2026 she joined Reps. Ocasio-Cortez and Summer Lee on a 'Toxic Tour' of South Memphis that stopped at Elon Musk's xAI Colossus data center, where the group held a press event calling for oversight, and she voted against the GOP SPEED Act permitting bill. No detailed data center statement in her own words was found.

evidence.title: MLK50 coverage: Pressley joins 'Toxic Tour' of Southwest Memphis including xAI's Colossus 1 data center
evidence.quote: Gas turbines are seen during a press conference in front of xAI’s data center after a toxic tour through Southwest Memphis.
evidence.what_it_shows: She toured pollution sites around the xAI data center with residents and appeared at a press conference there, aligning with critics of the project.

evidence.title: House roll call 356 (Dec 18 2025): H.R.4776 SPEED Act permitting reform, Pressley voted Nay
evidence.what_it_shows: She voted against the Republican permitting bill that supporters said would speed energy and data center projects.

ai_risk.summary: Pressley wants binding rules now. She co-leads the AI Civil Rights Act, which would ban discriminatory AI and require testing before and after deployment, backs the Algorithmic Accountability Act, and has long pushed a moratorium on government facial recognition. She frames unregulated AI as corporations experimenting on the public, especially Black and marginalized communities.

evidence.title: House Oversight hearing remarks: Pressley emphasizes need to regulate AI
evidence.quote: they’re offering the American people up as guinea pigs for corporations to conduct AI experiments with no oversight, no regulation, and no enforcement.
evidence.what_it_shows: She attacked the lack of AI oversight and called for regulation, accountability and civil rights enforcement over AI.

evidence.title: Press release: Pressley, Clarke, Markey reintroduce the AI Civil Rights Act
evidence.quote: We cannot allow AI to be the latest chapter in America’s history of exploiting marginalized people.
evidence.what_it_shows: She is a House co-lead of a comprehensive bill banning discriminatory AI and mandating pre- and post-deployment testing.

evidence.title: House Financial Services hearing remarks: Pressley calls for new civil rights protections in the age of AI
evidence.quote: We must not allow AI innovation without AI protections.
evidence.what_it_shows: She pressed witnesses to agree AI that discriminates should be prohibited and that algorithms should be assessed before use on the public.

evidence.title: 119th H.R.5511 Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would make companies test automated decision systems for bias and harm and report to the FTC.

evidence.title: 119th H.R.6356 Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025 (cosponsor and House co-lead)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would ban AI discrimination and require companies to check their AI before and after deployment.

evidence.title: 119th H.R.3060 No Biometric Barriers to Housing Act of 2025 (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would ban facial recognition in government-supported housing, a bill she has championed since 2019.

evidence.title: Press release: Pressley, Jayapal, Markey, Merkley reintroduce the Facial Recognition and Biometric Technology Moratorium Act
evidence.quote: Facial recognition technology is fundamentally flawed, systemically biased, and disproportionately targets Black and brown communities that are already over-surveilled and overpoliced
evidence.what_it_shows: She wants a pause on federal use of facial recognition and other biometric AI until Congress acts.

evidence.title: Letter from Reps. Pressley and Waters urging HUD to prohibit biased surveillance technology in federally assisted housing
evidence.quote: your agency must act in this critical moment to ensure public housing and HUD-assisted housing residents are not targeted by these discriminatory surveillance systems
evidence.what_it_shows: She pressed a federal agency to stop using facial recognition on public housing residents.

evidence.title: House Oversight subcommittee remarks: Pressley calls for Congress to address AI risks to marginalized communities
evidence.quote: Congress has been slow to act, forcing the Biden-Harris Administration to take executive action to enforce standards and guardrails.
evidence.what_it_shows: She defended the Biden AI executive order against overreach claims and urged Congress to legislate against biased algorithms.

tech_regulation.summary: Pressley voted against the 2024 TikTok bill because she wants comprehensive data privacy rules for all social media companies rather than a ban on one app, and she has backed reproductive data privacy and raised alarms about deepfake pornography harming girls. She has not led on antitrust or Section 230.

evidence.title: Press release: Pressley's statement opposing bill to ban TikTok
evidence.quote: Congress should pass comprehensive data privacy legislation that creates standards and regulations around data harvesting across all social media companies
evidence.what_it_shows: She opposed singling out TikTok and called for a holistic approach to regulating big tech and protecting data privacy.

evidence.title: House roll call 86 (Mar 13 2024): H.R.7521 TikTok divestiture bill, Pressley voted Nay
evidence.what_it_shows: She was one of the Democrats voting against forcing TikTok's sale, citing First Amendment and process concerns in her statement.

evidence.title: House Oversight hearing remarks: Pressley on non-consensual deepfake pornography and childhood trauma
evidence.quote: And as this report makes plain and this hearing has confirmed, our girls are being traumatized.
evidence.what_it_shows: She treats AI deepfake pornography as a child safety harm that needs a government response.

evidence.title: 118th H.R.3420 My Body, My Data Act of 2023 (cosponsor)
evidence.what_it_shows: Would stop apps and companies from collecting or sharing reproductive health data without a good reason.

preemption.summary: Pressley attacked the House GOP's 10-year ban on state AI laws in a June 2025 hearing, entering a Massachusetts legislature letter on its dangers into the record, and she signed the Nov 26 2025 letter from 81 House Democrats opposing any revival of the moratorium in the NDAA or by executive order.

evidence.title: House Oversight hearing remarks: Pressley criticizes the reconciliation bill's 10-year ban on state AI regulation
evidence.quote: Just two weeks ago, Republicans passed a reconciliation bill that would ban all states from regulating AI for 10 years.
evidence.what_it_shows: She condemned the state AI law moratorium and entered a Massachusetts Joint Committee letter detailing its dangers into the record.

evidence.title: Matsui-led letter from 81 House Democrats to Johnson, Thune, Jeffries and Schumer opposing an AI moratorium in the NDAA and a preemption executive order (Pressley signed)
evidence.quote: Congress should not freeze state and local AI safeguards, least of all when there are no meaningful federal protections in place.
evidence.what_it_shows: She is a confirmed signer (checked in the PDF text) of the main House Democratic letter defending states' ability to regulate AI.

china_chips.summary: Searched for statements on Nvidia chip sales, export controls, DeepSeek and the Chip Security Act and found nothing. Her only China-related tech vote was against the 2024 TikTok bill, which she called the wrong approach.

signature: House co-lead of the AI Civil Rights Act and longtime sponsor of a federal facial recognition moratorium; treats AI regulation as a civil rights fight for Black and marginalized communities and attacked the GOP's 10-year ban on state AI laws.

notable_quote.text: they’re offering the American people up as guinea pigs for corporations to conduct AI experiments with no oversight, no regulation, and no enforcement.

groups: House Financial Services Committee Bipartisan Working Group on Artificial Intelligence (118th Congress, member; confirmed in her Mar 21 2024 hearing remarks)
search_notes: Ran about 14 Google News queries (AI, data centers, chatbot/deepfake/Big Tech/TikTok, facial recognition/algorithms, Nvidia/export controls, moratorium/preemption/executive order, KOSA, Memphis xAI, Leading the Future, Financial Services AI hearings, utility bills) plus a full archived listing of pressley.house.gov. Opened and quoted six of her own press releases and hearing transcripts (Jun 5 2025, Dec 3 2025, Dec 11 2025, Mar 21 2024, Mar 13 2024, Mar 12 2024, Mar 7 2023, May 26 2023). Extracted the Matsui letter PDF text and confirmed her signature; confirmed she is NOT on the Clarke Dec 3 2025 NDAA letter or the Casar Aug 2026 AI CEO letter. Verified TikTok (Nay) and SPEED Act (Nay) votes on govtrack. For the July 2026 Memphis xAI visit, the localmemphis.com, WREG and Politico pages returned 403 errors, so the MLK50 story is the only opened source and no direct Pressley quote on data centers was captured; the data center score is therefore low confidence. She is also an original cosponsor of the Energy Bills Relief Act (H.R.7977), but the bill's data center content could not be confirmed, so it was not used. She sits on the Financial Services subcommittee on Digital Assets, Financial Technology, and Artificial Intelligence as a member, not in a leadership role.
